definitions.meaning: The quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price.
The quantity of a good firms are willing and able to offer for sale at each price.
The point where supply and demand cross, so quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.
A non-price factor, such as consumer income, that changes how much buyers want at every price.
A good buyers want more of when their income rises.
A movement of the whole demand curve, caused by a change in a condition of demand.
A change in quantity caused only by a change in the good's own price, sliding along an unchanged curve.
The gap at a price where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
The amount buyers want at one particular price, read off the demand curve.
The amount firms offer at one particular price, read off the supply curve.

mechanismSteps: Equilibrium: supply and demand cross at E1, at price P1 and quantity Q1 (s1).
The shift: consumer income rises for a normal good, so the whole demand curve shifts right from D1 to D2 while supply does not move (s2).
The shortage: at the old price P1, quantity demanded Qd exceeds quantity supplied Qs, so a shortage opens (s3).
The new equilibrium: competing buyers bid the price up along the unchanged supply curve until the shortage closes at E2, price P2 and quantity Q2 (s4).
objectives: Describe the starting equilibrium where supply and demand cross
Explain why a rise in income shifts the whole demand curve right
Link the shortage at the old price and the price rise into one causal chain to the new equilibrium
subject: economics
title: Demand and supply: an income rise bids the price up

trap.explanation: The slip: The quantity gets bigger either way, so a shift of the curve and a movement along it look like the same thing. The fix: A change in a condition of demand such as income shifts the whole demand curve; only a change in the good's own price moves along it - the shift opens a shortage at the old price, and competition bids the price up along supply to the new equilibrium. In class, replay scene 2: freeze the market at the old price P1 and ask how quantity demanded can be Qd if buyers are still on the same curve - it cannot, so the curve itself must have shifted.
trap.misconception: Higher income just slides buyers along the same demand curve to a bigger quantity.

workedExample: Test the slide claim on this market. Step 1 (s2): at the old price P1, buyers now want Qd rather than Q1, so demand at an unchanged price has changed - a slide along the same curve cannot do that. Step 2 (s3): the shift opens a shortage at P1. Step 3 (s4): competition bids the price up along supply until the shortage closes at the new equilibrium. So the driver is a shift of the whole demand curve, not a slide along it.
